finding: `node atm.mjs git commit --dry-run` and the real pre-commit hook can disagree about active foreign governance residue ownership.
expectedBehavior: The same ownership proof rules must be shared by the commit bundle builder and pre-commit hook: active direction lock or active ledger claim should protect non-staged foreign governance residue from blocking another active task, while orphan residue stays fail-closed.
evidenceOrRepro: Closed 2026-09-03 after current-source verification. `tests/cli/git-commit-task-scoped-staging.test.ts` exercises two active claims and direction locks: a foreign active staged entry remains blocked without an explicit stage-override lease, an authorized bounded commit preserves and restores the foreign index entry, and the current task commit excludes it. The same suite proves dry-run and real commit both tolerate and defer an unrelated foreign bundle manifest without absorbing it. `tests/cli/protected-override-audit-direction-lock.test.ts` proves the real pre-commit hook admits only the current task's protected audit under its active direction lock and remains fail-closed for the foreign audit. `packages/cli/src/commands/git-governance/implementation/commit-bundle-resolution.test.ts` covers unstaged and stale-index foreign manifests. All focused tests passed on 2026-09-03.
followUp: No source repair remains for the reported wrapper/pre-commit ownership disagreement. Keep the existing parity suites in the Git governance regression family; reopen only with a new reproducer where their candidate decisions diverge.
